Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the MCAS procedure library across all conduct areas (claims, underwriting, marketing/sales, complaints, producer licensing, cancellation/nonrenewal); escalates to Head of Compliance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Kentucky Revised Statutes Chapter 304 (unfair claims settlement and trade practices sections) plus the current-year NAIC MCAS Data Call & Definitions Handbook, re-read at each annual review (rep: Kentucky KRS Chapter 304)

In-scope processes.value: Claims handling, underwriting/rate & form actions, marketing & advertising review, complaint intake & resolution, producer appointment/termination, and policy cancellation/nonrenewal, for every MCAS-reportable LOB (private passenger auto, homeowners, other liability, life, annuity, LTC/DI, LPI, fraternal, short-term limited duration health, travel) across the 34 MCAS-participating jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: NAIC MCAS Data Call template/system defines the interrogatories the procedures must map to; procedure library and version history live in the GRC platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: One written procedure per conduct area (Claims Handling, Underwriting & Rating, Marketing & Sales, Grievance & Complaint Handling, Producer Licensing/Termination, Policy Servicing) mapped 1:1 to the current-year NAIC MCAS interrogatory set and Definitions document by LOB

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Head of Compliance and the LOB business owner (Chief Claims Officer, Chief Underwriting Officer, Chief Marketing Officer as applicable); re-approved annually or on any NAIC MCAS Handbook data-element change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual review cycle closes procedures 60 days ahead of the earliest MCAS submission deadline (April 30 for P&C lines, June 30 for Life/Annuity/LTC/DI lines) so the reporting team works from a current procedure set

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC platform sends 90/60/30-day review-due alerts to each conduct-area procedure owner ahead of the annual MCAS Handbook release (typically published in Q4 for the following filing year)

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed procedure PDFs, version history and the mapped interrogatory cross-reference retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any conduct area found without a current procedure, or with a procedure that no longer maps to the current Handbook, is logged as an exception with root cause and a remediation owner/date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every procedure gap before the next MCAS filing opens

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All six conduct-area procedures crossed with every MCAS-reportable LOB the company writes for the current filing year

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance for missing citation sign-off or a missing interrogatory-to-step mapping; any procedure not re-approved within 12 months is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is an annual review; test runs once per cycle immediately after the annual approval close date

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have authored or approved any sampled procedure

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual procedure-maintenance test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Signed procedures, citation sign-offs and approval chain, presentable as a market conduct exam response within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager owns the exam/inquiry response on procedures; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of a procedure gap before it is sent

checklist.step: Pull the current-year NAIC MCAS Handbook and Data Call definitions
actions: Download the current-year NAIC MCAS Data Call & Definitions Handbook and the LOB-specific interrogatory set for every MCAS-reportable line the company writes (auto, homeowners, other liability, life, annuity, LTC, DI, LPI, fraternal, STLD health, travel).
Compare the new Handbook's data element list line-by-line against last year's using the NAIC's published Handbook change summary, or a manual diff if none is issued.
Highlight every new, removed or redefined data element and route it to the conduct-area owner it affects.
File the current Handbook PDF and the diff notes in the procedure library folder for the year.
checklist.done: the current Handbook, the LOB interrogatory sets and a documented diff against last year are on file.

checklist.step: Inventory the conduct areas and confirm one procedure owner per area
actions: List the six MCAS conduct areas — Claims Handling, Underwriting & Rating, Marketing & Sales, Grievance/Complaint Handling, Producer Licensing & Termination, Policy Servicing/Cancellation-Nonrenewal — against the LOBs the company writes.

Confirm a named business owner for each area: Chief Claims Officer (claims), Chief Underwriting Officer (underwriting), Chief Marketing Officer (marketing), Complaints Manager (grievance), Producer Licensing Coordinator (producer), Policy Admin Ops Lead (servicing).
Where an owner has changed since last year, get written confirmation of the new owner from Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every conduct area has a named, confirmed owner recorded in the procedure library.

checklist.step: Draft or update each conduct-area procedure against the current interrogatories
actions: For each conduct area, open last year's approved procedure and mark it up against the current Handbook's interrogatory wording.

Add a cross-reference table mapping each procedure step to the specific MCAS data element(s) it produces (e.g., claim received date, claim closed date, complaint received date, complaint closure category).
Write the data source and system of record for each element next to the mapping (e.g., claim dates from the Claims Platform, complaint dates from the workflow/case management tool).
Route the marked-up draft to the conduct-area business owner for line edits.
checklist.done: each conduct-area procedure has a current draft with a complete element-to-source mapping table.

checklist.step: Validate the citations behind each procedure
actions: Re-read the state unfair claims settlement practices act, unfair trade practices act and market conduct examination statute for the representative jurisdiction (Kentucky KRS Chapter 304) and confirm the procedure still reflects current law.
Spot-check two additional MCAS-participating states (Louisiana RS Title 22 and Massachusetts M.G.L. Chapters 174-176) for material differences in complaint-handling or claims-timeliness standards.
Note any state-specific deviation directly on the procedure as a callout box.
Sign and date the citation-verification line on the procedure cover sheet.
checklist.done: counsel has signed a dated citation-verification line on every conduct-area procedure.

checklist.step: Confirm the in-scope systems list for each conduct area
actions: For each data element in the mapping table, trace it to the source system (Claims Platform, Policy Administration Platform, workflow/case management tool, agency/producer management system).
Confirm the extract used for MCAS reporting pulls from the system of record, not a manually maintained spreadsheet, unless no system source exists.
Where a manual spreadsheet is still the source, flag it to Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager as a data-quality risk.
Record the confirmed system list on the procedure's in-scope-systems line.
checklist.done: every data element's source system is confirmed and listed, with manual-spreadsheet sources flagged as risks.

checklist.step: Route each procedure for business-owner approval
actions: Send each conduct-area procedure to its named business owner with a 10-business-day review SLA.
Track outstanding reviews in the procedure library's approval workflow.
Escalate any owner past the SLA to Head of Compliance.
Log the approval date and approver name on the procedure cover sheet once returned.
checklist.done: every conduct-area procedure carries a dated business-owner approval within the SLA or a logged escalation.

checklist.step: Obtain Head of Compliance final sign-off
actions: Review the full procedure set for internal consistency — that claims, underwriting, marketing, complaint, producer and servicing procedures do not conflict on shared definitions (e.g., a 'complaint' must be defined the same way across areas).
Confirm counsel's citation sign-off and the business-owner approvals are all present.
Sign and date the master approval page covering all six conduct-area procedures.
checklist.done: Head of Compliance has signed the master approval page for the full annual procedure set.

checklist.step: Publish the approved procedures to the GRC platform
actions: Upload each signed procedure PDF to the GRC platform's policy library under the current filing year folder.
Set the review-due date to 12 months from approval and attach it to the record.
Retire the prior year's procedure version to the archive while preserving version history.
Notify each conduct-area owner and the Regulatory Reporting team that the current procedure is live.
checklist.done: the current-year procedure set is published in the GRC platform with an active review-due date and the prior version archived.

checklist.step: Train conduct-area staff on any changed steps
actions: Identify every procedure step that changed from last year using the redline.
Hold a briefing with each conduct area's operational lead (Claims Director / Manager, UW Operations Manager, Complaints Manager, Producer Licensing Coordinator) covering only the changed steps.
Circulate a one-page change summary by email to the affected teams.
Log attendance and the briefing date.
checklist.done: a documented briefing and attendance log exists for every changed procedure step.

checklist.step: Confirm deadline tracking is wired into the annual calendar
actions: Add the procedure's own review-due date and the downstream MCAS submission deadlines (April 30 P&C, June 30 Life/Annuity/LTC/DI) to the compliance master calendar.
Confirm the calendar entry links back to the GRC platform procedure record.
Verify reminder rules are attached to each entry.
checklist.done: the master compliance calendar carries the procedure review date and both MCAS submission deadlines, linked to the GRC record.

checklist.step: Set the 90/60/30-day review reminders
actions: In the GRC platform, configure automated alerts at 90, 60 and 30 days before the procedure's review-due date, addressed to the conduct-area owner and Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
Test one alert by temporarily adjusting a due date in a sandbox record and confirming delivery.
Restore the live due date after the test.
checklist.done: the 90/60/30-day alert chain is configured and proven to fire on the live procedure records.

checklist.step: Cross-check the procedures against last year's exam and complaint findings
actions: Pull any market conduct exam findings and regulator complaint-ratio flags received in the prior 12 months.
Confirm each finding maps to a corrective step now present in the relevant conduct-area procedure.
Flag any finding with no corresponding procedure update to Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: every prior-year exam or complaint finding is traced to a procedure update, or logged as an open gap.

checklist.step: File the evidence package in the compliance evidence repository
actions: Assemble the signed procedures, counsel citation sign-offs, business-owner approvals and the Head of Compliance master approval page.
Upload the package to the compliance evidence repository under the current filing year, tagged by conduct area and LOB.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
checklist.done: the full evidence package is filed, tagged and retention-labelled in the repository.

checklist.step: Log any conduct area left without a current procedure as an exception
actions: At the annual review close date, list any conduct area still on the prior-year procedure or with no procedure at all.
Open a tracker issue per gap with root cause (owner turnover, Handbook change missed, resourcing) and an assigned remediator.
Set a remediation date no later than 30 days before the earliest MCAS submission deadline.
checklist.done: every unresolved procedure gap has a tracker issue with root cause, owner and a remediation date ahead of the filing deadline.

checklist.step: Close the annual cycle with Head of Compliance sign-off on remediation
actions: Review the exception log for the cycle and confirm every gap is either closed or has an approved, dated remediation plan.
Sign the annual procedure-maintenance closure memo.
File the closure memo alongside the evidence package.
checklist.done: Head of Compliance has signed a closure memo confirming every exception is closed or has a dated remediation plan.

testing.step: Build the population of conduct areas and LOBs due for review
actions: List every conduct area (6) crossed with every MCAS-reportable LOB the company writes, from the current Handbook's LOB list.
Reconcile the LOB list to the company's NAIC Annual Statement lines of business to confirm nothing MCAS-reportable is missing.
Document the reconciled population count and source.
testing.done: the conduct-area x LOB population is reconciled to the Annual Statement LOB list and documented.

testing.step: Sample procedures for independent re-review
actions: Select all conduct areas with a prior-year exam or complaint finding, plus a random sample of at least 3 additional conduct area/LOB combinations.
Record the seed and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers every prior-finding area plus a documented random selection, reproducible from the recorded seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the citation check independently
actions: Without reading the procedure's cited sections first, independently research the current unfair claims settlement, unfair trade practices and market conduct exam statutes for the representative state on each sampled row.
Compare your independent citation to what the procedure cites; any mismatch is an exception, including a right conclusion with a stale or wrong cite.
testing.done: each sampled procedure has an independent citation re-check with any mismatch logged.

testing.step: Confirm the interrogatory-to-procedure-step mapping on the sample
actions: Open the current NAIC MCAS interrogatory set for the sampled LOB in the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) system.
For each sampled procedure, trace every interrogatory data element back to a named procedure step and system source.
Flag any interrogatory element with no corresponding procedure step.
testing.done: every sampled procedure's interrogatory elements trace to a named step and source system, or are logged as gaps.

testing.step: Verify approval evidence on the sample
actions: In the GRC platform, open each sampled procedure record and confirm counsel citation sign-off, business-owner approval and Head of Compliance master sign-off are all present and dated in the correct order.
Confirm the review-due date is set to 12 months from approval.
testing.done: approval sequence and dates are confirmed present and correctly ordered for every sampled procedure.

testing.step: Test that the 90/60/30-day reminder configuration actually fires
actions: Pull the GRC platform's alert log for the sampled records and confirm 90/60/30-day alerts were sent to the correct owner.
For any record missing an alert, check the configuration and log a system exception.
testing.done: alert logs confirm the 90/60/30-day chain fired for every sampled record, or a system exception is logged.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline math backing the review cycle
actions: For each sampled procedure, recompute the required review-close date as 60 days before the earliest applicable MCAS submission deadline (April 30 P&C / June 30 Life-Annuity-LTC-DI).
Compare to the actual approval date on file and flag any procedure approved after its required close date.
testing.done: recomputed review-close dates are compared to actual approval dates with any late approval flagged.

testing.step: Trace training evidence for changed steps on the sample
actions: For each sampled procedure with a redlined change, pull the training briefing log and attendance record.
Confirm the briefing occurred before the procedure's effective date and covered the operational lead for that conduct area.
testing.done: training evidence pre-dating the effective date is confirmed for every sampled changed procedure.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every citation mismatch, mapping gap, missing approval, missing alert or late training identified in testing.
Assign root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date ahead of the next MCAS submission deadline.
Carry any open issue into the next cycle's mandatory retest.
testing.done: every finding has a tracker issue with root cause, owner and a remediation date, carried to retest if open.

testing.step: Conclude and sign the test
actions: Compute the exception rate across the sample and compare to a zero-tolerance threshold for missing citation sign-off or missing interrogatory mapping.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the workpaper evidence.
Have an independent reviewer who authored none of the sampled procedures sign the workpaper and file it in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed in the compliance evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual MCAS build-validate-submit cycle across all reportable LOBs and the 34 participating jurisdictions; escalates blocking data issues to Head of Compliance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Massachusetts General Laws Chapters 174 to 176 market-conduct/data-call authority plus the current-year NAIC MCAS Data Call Handbook, re-read at each filing cycle (rep: Massachusetts M.G.L. Chapters 174-176)

In-scope processes.value: Data extraction, validation, jurisdiction-level aggregation and submission of MCAS interrogatory responses for every reportable LOB and every one of the 34 participating states

In-scope systems.value: NAIC MCAS Data Call submission system; source extracts drawn from Claims Platform, Policy Administration Platform and the workflow/case management tool

Compliance procedure documented.value: MCAS Submission Procedure — extract build, validation edit checks, state-by-state review, sign-off and NAIC system submission

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Head of Compliance; reviewed annually against the current MCAS Handbook

Deadline reminders configured.value: T-60/T-30/T-10 business day reminders to Regulatory Reporting Analyst and Head of Compliance ahead of each LOB's deadline

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Submission extracts, validation logs, sign-offs and the NAIC confirmation receipt retained 7 years

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late or amended MCAS submission before resubmission

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance for missed deadlines; validation edit-check failure rate must be zero at final submission; any post-submission amendment is a fail requiring root cause

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built or validated any sampled submission

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual MCAS submission test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: NAIC confirmation receipts, validation logs and the submitted extract, presentable to a state market conduct examiner within 5 business days

checklist.step: Confirm the current-year MCAS Data Call template and LOB scope
actions: Download the current-year NAIC MCAS Data Call template and the Standard Data Record (SDR) layout for each reportable LOB.
Confirm which of the 34 participating states apply to each LOB the company writes, using the NAIC's current MCAS participating-states list.
Note any new or dropped data elements against last year's template.
File the template and states list in the submission working folder.
checklist.done: the current template, participating-states list and element diff are on file for every reportable LOB.

checklist.step: Extract the raw source data by LOB and state
actions: Pull claims counts, closed-without-payment counts and average days-to-close from the Claims Platform for each reportable LOB and state.
Pull new business, renewal, cancellation and nonrenewal counts from the Policy Administration Platform.
Pull complaint counts and resolution categories from the workflow/case management tool.
Pull producer appointment/termination counts from the agency/producer management system for LOBs with producer-related MCAS questions.
Land all extracts in the MCAS staging schema tagged by LOB, state and reporting period.
checklist.done: all four source extracts are landed in the staging schema, tagged by LOB, state and period.

checklist.step: Map extracted fields to MCAS Standard Data Record elements
actions: For each SDR element, confirm the staging field that feeds it and the transformation logic (e.g., days-to-close = claim closed date minus claim received date).
Document any element with no direct source and the manual workaround used.
Have the conduct-area business owner (Chief Claims Officer, Chief Underwriting Officer) confirm the mapping for their area in writing.
checklist.done: every SDR element has a documented source mapping, confirmed by the relevant business owner.

checklist.step: Run the NAIC validation edit checks on the draft submission
actions: Load the mapped data into the MCAS submission tool's validation/edit-check function.
Resolve every failed edit check (e.g., closed counts exceeding received counts, negative days-to-close) before proceeding.
Re-run validation until zero edit-check failures remain.
Save the clean validation log.
checklist.done: the draft submission passes all NAIC edit checks with a saved, zero-failure validation log.

checklist.step: Reconcile submission totals to internal source-of-record reports
actions: Compare total claims counts in the draft submission to the Claims Platform's own management reporting for the same period.
Compare complaint counts to the workflow/case management tool's quarterly summary report.
Investigate and document any variance greater than 1%.
checklist.done: submission totals reconcile to internal source reports within 1%, with variances documented.

checklist.step: Route the state-level draft to conduct-area owners for review
actions: Send each conduct area's state-by-state figures to its business owner (Chief Claims Officer, Chief Underwriting Officer, Complaints Manager, Producer Licensing Coordinator) for a plausibility review against their operational reporting.
Set a 5-business-day review SLA ahead of the submission deadline.
Log sign-off or requested corrections per owner.
checklist.done: every conduct-area owner has signed off or requested corrections on their state-level figures within the SLA.

checklist.step: Apply corrections and re-validate
actions: Incorporate every business-owner correction into the staging data.
Re-run the mapping and NAIC edit checks after corrections.
Confirm the correction is reflected before closing the correction ticket.
checklist.done: all business-owner corrections are applied and the resubmitted draft passes edit checks.

checklist.step: Obtain Regulatory Reporting Manager and Head of Compliance final sign-off
actions: Assemble the final validated submission package with the reconciliation notes and business-owner sign-offs.
Present to Head of Compliance for final review, focused on any state with a prior-year exam or outlier flag.
Obtain a dated sign-off before the submission window opens.
checklist.done: Head of Compliance has signed off the final validated package before submission.

checklist.step: Submit the MCAS data through the NAIC system by the LOB deadline
actions: Log in to the NAIC MCAS Data Call submission system and select the current filing year and company NAIC group/co-code.
Upload the final SDR file for each LOB, selecting every applicable state from the 34 participating jurisdictions.
Submit before the LOB deadline — April 30 for P&C lines, June 30 for Life/Annuity/LTC/DI — and capture the on-screen confirmation number and timestamp.
Download the confirmation receipt PDF for each LOB submitted.
checklist.done: every reportable LOB is submitted before its deadline with a captured confirmation number and receipt.

checklist.step: File the submission confirmation and evidence package
actions: Upload the confirmation receipts, final SDR files, validation logs and business-owner sign-offs to the compliance evidence repository under the filing year.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Index the package by LOB and state for retrieval.
checklist.done: the full submission evidence package is filed, retention-labelled and indexed by LOB and state.

checklist.step: Monitor for NAIC rejection or resubmission notices
actions: Check the MCAS submission system's status screen daily for 10 business days after submission for rejection or amendment-request flags.
For any rejection, identify the failing element, correct the source data and resubmit within 5 business days.
Log the resubmission confirmation number.
checklist.done: submission status is confirmed clean, or any rejection is corrected and resubmitted within 5 business days with a logged confirmation.

checklist.step: Update the compliance master calendar with actual submission dates
actions: Record the actual submission date and confirmation number for each LOB against the planned deadline in the compliance master calendar.
Flag any LOB submitted after its deadline for the exception log regardless of reason.
checklist.done: actual submission dates and confirmation numbers are recorded against every planned deadline in the calendar.

checklist.step: Brief Market Conduct Compliance on outlier risk from the submitted data
actions: Compare the company's submitted ratios (e.g., complaint ratio, claims closed-without-payment ratio) against publicly available NAIC MCAS benchmark ranges where published.
Flag any state/LOB combination trending toward an outlier range to Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
Document the comparison and the flags raised.
checklist.done: submitted ratios are compared to available benchmarks with any outlier risk flagged and documented.

checklist.step: Log any late, rejected or amended submission as an exception
actions: Open a tracker issue for any LOB/state missing its deadline, rejected, or requiring a post-submission amendment.
Assign root cause (data source delay, edit-check failure unresolved, mapping error) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and a process-improvement action for next year's cycle.
checklist.done: every late, rejected or amended submission has a tracker issue with root cause, owner and a remediation/process-improvement action.

checklist.step: Close the cycle with Head of Compliance sign-off
actions: Review the full-year submission status across all LOBs and states, including any exceptions.
Sign the annual MCAS submission closure memo confirming completeness or listing open items with dates.
File the closure memo with the evidence package.
checklist.done: Head of Compliance has signed the annual closure memo covering every LOB and state, filed with the evidence package.

testing.step: Build the population of required LOB/state submissions
actions: From the current NAIC MCAS participating-states list and the company's written LOBs, build the full population of required LOB x state submissions for the filing year.
Reconcile the population to the company's Annual Statement Schedule T premium-by-state to confirm no in-scope state/LOB is missing.
testing.done: the required-submission population is reconciled to Schedule T and documented.

testing.step: Reconcile submitted confirmations to the required population
actions: Match each required LOB/state combination to a submission confirmation number and date.
List any unmatched combination as an automatic exception, including anything submitted after its deadline.
testing.done: every required combination is matched to a confirmation or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of LOB/state combinations flagged as outlier risk or with a prior-year exam finding.
Take a random sample of at least 10 additional combinations, seeded and reproducible.
Record the seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all outlier-flagged and prior-finding combinations.

testing.step: Re-perform the source-to-SDR mapping on the sample
actions: For each sampled combination, independently trace the submitted SDR values back to the Claims Platform, Policy Administration Platform or workflow/case management tool extract.
Recompute at least one derived field (e.g., days-to-close) directly from source dates and compare to the submitted value.
Log any variance as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled value is independently traced and one derived field recomputed, with variances logged.

testing.step: Re-run the NAIC edit checks independently on the sample
actions: Re-load the sampled combinations' source data into the MCAS validation tool independent of the original build.
Confirm zero edit-check failures reproduce the original validation log.
Flag any discrepancy between the independent run and the filed validation log.
testing.done: independent edit-check runs match the filed validation log for every sampled combination, or discrepancies are logged.

testing.step: Trace confirmation receipts to the NAIC system
actions: Log in to the MCAS submission system's status/history screen and pull the actual submission record for each sampled combination.
Compare the system's timestamp and confirmation number to the receipt filed as evidence.
Confirm the submission date is before the LOB's regulatory deadline.
testing.done: every sampled combination's system record matches its filed receipt and pre-dates the deadline.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline compliance across the full population
actions: Compare every population row's actual submission timestamp to its LOB deadline (April 30 P&C / June 30 Life-Annuity-LTC-DI).
List every row submitted on or after the deadline as a breach, not a documentation exception.
testing.done: deadline compliance is computed for 100% of the population with any breach separately identified.

testing.step: Verify business-owner and Head of Compliance sign-off evidence on the sample
actions: Confirm each sampled combination's evidence package contains a dated business-owner review and Head of Compliance final sign-off pre-dating the submission.
Flag any missing or out-of-sequence sign-off.
testing.done: sign-off sequencing and dating are confirmed for every sampled combination, or gaps are flagged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every mapping variance, edit-check discrepancy, missing sign-off or deadline breach found.
Assign root cause and owner; deadline breaches route directly to Head of Compliance for a self-assessment of regulatory exposure.
Set remediation dates and carry open issues into next cycle's mandatory retest.
testing.done: every finding has a tracker issue with root cause, owner, remediation date, and breaches carry a self-assessment.

testing.step: Conclude and sign the test
actions: Compute the exception and breach rate against the zero-missed-deadline threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and have an independent reviewer who performed none of the sampled re-performances sign the workpaper.
Report results and any breach to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed in the compliance evidence repository.

checklist.step: Confirm the benchmark set for the quarter
actions: Pull the most recently published NAIC Market Regulation Handbook outlier/benchmark guidance and any state-specific market analysis thresholds for the representative states.
Confirm no benchmark has changed since last quarter; if changed, update the monitoring procedure's threshold table.
Document the benchmark source and effective date for the quarter.
checklist.done: the quarter's benchmark set is confirmed current and documented with its source and effective date.

checklist.step: Extract quarterly source data by LOB and state
actions: Pull claims received, closed and closed-without-payment counts from the Claims Platform for the quarter, by LOB and state.
Pull new business, cancellation and nonrenewal counts from the Policy Administration Platform.
Pull complaint counts and categories from the workflow/case management tool.
Land the extracts in the metrics staging area tagged by LOB, state and quarter.
checklist.done: all three source extracts are landed and tagged by LOB, state and quarter.

checklist.step: Calculate the ratio metrics
actions: Compute complaint ratio = complaints received divided by policies in force (per 1,000), by LOB and state.
Compute claims closed-without-payment ratio = CWOP claims divided by total closed claims, by LOB and state.
Compute average days-to-close = mean(claim closed date minus claim received date), by LOB and state.
Compute cancellation/nonrenewal ratio = cancellations plus nonrenewals divided by policies in force, by LOB and state.
Publish the ratios to the quarterly metrics dashboard in the BI/reporting platform.
checklist.done: all four ratio metrics are calculated and published to the dashboard by LOB and state.

checklist.step: Compare metrics to benchmark ranges
actions: For each LOB/state, compare the quarter's ratios to the confirmed benchmark range and to the company's own trailing 4-quarter trend.
Flag any metric outside its benchmark range or moving more than one standard deviation from the trailing trend.
Color-code the dashboard (green/amber/red) to reflect the comparison.
checklist.done: every LOB/state ratio is compared to benchmark and trend, with out-of-range metrics flagged and color-coded.

checklist.step: Investigate each flagged metric's root cause
actions: For each flagged metric, pull the underlying transaction-level detail from the source system (e.g., the specific complaints or claims driving the ratio).
Interview the relevant operational owner (Claims Director / Manager, UW Operations Manager) on any process or staffing change that quarter.
Document a root cause hypothesis for each flag: volume shift, process change, data quality issue, or genuine conduct deterioration.
checklist.done: every flagged metric has a documented root-cause investigation and hypothesis.

checklist.step: Distinguish data-quality flags from genuine conduct flags
actions: Re-check the source extract for the flagged LOB/state for known data issues (duplicate records, missing close dates, miscoded state).
Correct and re-run the ratio calculation if a data issue is confirmed.
Confirm in writing to Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager whether the flag is data-quality or genuine.
checklist.done: every flag is confirmed as data-quality (corrected and recalculated) or genuine conduct, in writing.

checklist.step: Escalate genuine conduct outliers
actions: For each confirmed genuine outlier, brief the LOB business owner and Head of Compliance within 5 business days of confirmation.
Request a written explanation and a proposed corrective action from the business owner.
Log the escalation date and recipients.
checklist.done: every confirmed genuine outlier is escalated within 5 business days with a logged date and recipient list.

checklist.step: Build the corrective action plan for sustained outliers
actions: Where a metric is outside benchmark for a second consecutive quarter, require the business owner to submit a written corrective action plan with named actions, owners and target dates.
Review the plan for adequacy against the root cause identified.
Track the plan's actions in the GRC platform against their target dates.
checklist.done: every second-consecutive-quarter outlier has a tracked corrective action plan with named owners and dates.

checklist.step: Publish the quarterly conduct metrics report
actions: Compile the quarter's dashboard, root-cause notes and any corrective action plans into the quarterly conduct metrics report.
Distribute to Head of Compliance and the Compliance Committee within 15 business days of quarter close.
Archive the report with the underlying data extract.
checklist.done: the quarterly report is distributed within 15 business days and archived with its underlying data.

checklist.step: Present outlier trends to the Compliance Committee
actions: Present the quarter's flagged metrics, root causes and corrective action status to the Compliance Committee.
Record committee questions and any additional action items in the meeting minutes.
Assign follow-up owners for any new action item.
checklist.done: the Compliance Committee has reviewed the quarter's outliers with minutes recording any new action items and owners.

checklist.step: Feed sustained outliers into the market-conduct exam readiness file
actions: For any LOB/state outside benchmark for two or more consecutive quarters, add the metric history and corrective action plan to that LOB/state's exam readiness file.
Note the linkage in the quarterly report so exam readiness stays current with monitoring results.
checklist.done: every sustained outlier's metric history and corrective action plan is added to the exam readiness file.

checklist.step: Confirm quarterly deadline tracking
actions: Confirm the quarter's report was published within the 15-business-day SLA in the compliance master calendar.
Log any late report with the reason.
checklist.done: the quarter's report publication date is logged against the 15-day SLA with any lateness explained.

checklist.step: Verify reminder configuration
actions: Confirm the T-10/T-5 business day reminder alerts are configured and were sent to the BI Developer and Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager ahead of the quarter's report date.
Correct the alert configuration if any reminder failed to send.
checklist.done: T-10/T-5 reminders are confirmed sent or the configuration is corrected.

checklist.step: File the quarterly evidence package
actions: Upload the quarterly report, dashboard export, root-cause notes and corrective action plans to the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label and index by LOB, state and quarter.
checklist.done: the quarterly evidence package is filed, retention-labelled and indexed.

checklist.step: Log unresolved outliers as exceptions
actions: Open a tracker issue for any metric outside benchmark with no corrective action plan by the report deadline.
Assign root cause, owner and a remediation date.
Require Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager sign-off before the issue closes.
checklist.done: every unresolved outlier has a tracker issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and a manager sign-off gate.

testing.step: Build the population of quarterly metric reports for the two most recent quarters
actions: Pull the last two quarterly conduct metrics reports and their underlying dashboard exports.
Reconcile the LOB/state coverage in each report to the company's full written book for that quarter.
testing.done: the two-quarter population is reconciled to the full written book for each quarter.

testing.step: Reconcile flagged outliers to escalation and corrective action records
actions: Match every metric flagged out-of-benchmark in either quarter to a logged escalation or corrective action plan.
List any flagged metric with no escalation record as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every flagged metric is matched to an escalation/corrective action record or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of metrics flagged out-of-benchmark in either of the two quarters.
Take a random sample of at least 8 in-benchmark metrics, seeded and reproducible.
Record the seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: the sample covers all flagged metrics plus a documented random selection of in-benchmark metrics.

testing.step: Re-perform the ratio calculation independently on the sample
actions: Pull the raw claims, policy and complaint counts independently from source systems for each sampled LOB/state/quarter.
Recompute each ratio metric using the documented formula and compare to the published dashboard value.
Log any variance beyond rounding as an exception.
testing.done: recomputed ratios match published values for every sampled metric, or variances are logged.

testing.step: Verify the benchmark comparison logic
actions: Confirm the benchmark range applied to each sampled metric matches the benchmark set documented for that quarter.
Recompute the color-code classification (green/amber/red) independently and compare to the dashboard.
testing.done: benchmark ranges and color-code classifications are independently confirmed for every sampled metric.

testing.step: Test root-cause documentation quality on flagged samples
actions: For each sampled flagged metric, confirm a documented root-cause investigation exists with named transaction-level detail reviewed and an operational owner interviewed.
Flag any root-cause note that is generic or unsupported by transaction-level detail.
testing.done: root-cause documentation for every sampled flag is confirmed specific and evidence-backed, or flagged as inadequate.

testing.step: Verify corrective action plans for sustained outliers
actions: For each sampled metric out-of-benchmark for two consecutive quarters, confirm a corrective action plan exists in the GRC platform with named actions, owners and target dates.
Check whether prior-quarter action items were completed on time.
testing.done: corrective action plans and their on-time completion are confirmed for every sampled sustained outlier.

testing.step: Recompute the reporting-deadline compliance
actions: Compare each quarter's actual report publication date to the 15-business-day SLA from quarter close.
List any late report and the stated reason.
testing.done: SLA compliance is recomputed for both quarters with any late report and its reason listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every calculation variance, benchmark misclassification, weak root-cause note, missing corrective action or late report.
Assign root cause and owner; set remediation dates.
Carry open issues into the next semi-annual retest.
testing.done: every finding has a tracker issue with root cause, owner and remediation date, carried to retest if open.

testing.step: Conclude and sign the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the two-consecutive-quarter-without-a-plan threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and have an independent reviewer who performed none of the sampled re-calculations sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is reported to the Compliance Committee and filed in the compliance evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the continuously maintained exam readiness file for every LOB/state combination, ready for a state market conduct examination on short notice

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Kentucky Revised Statutes Chapter 304 market conduct examination provisions, re-read whenever a state issues an exam call letter or updates its exam handbook (rep: Kentucky KRS Chapter 304)

In-scope processes.value: Continuous assembly and refresh of the exam readiness file — procedures, MCAS submissions, complaint logs, sample policy/claim files, producer files and prior exam responses — for every LOB/state combination

In-scope systems.value: Exam readiness files maintained in the GRC platform; source documents drawn from the Claims Platform, Policy Administration Platform, workflow/case management tool and agency/producer management system

Compliance procedure documented.value: Exam Readiness Maintenance Procedure — quarterly file refresh, document inventory checklist, ownership assignment, mock-exam self-test

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Head of Compliance; reviewed annually

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: No external deadline; internal quarterly refresh checkpoint plus an immediate refresh trigger on receipt of any exam call letter (states typically require a document response within 10-30 days of the call letter)

Deadline reminders configured.value: Quarterly refresh reminders to the exam readiness file owner; an immediate high-priority alert is configured to fire the same day any exam call letter is logged

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Exam readiness files and refresh logs retained 7 years, plus the full life of any open exam

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any LOB/state file found stale (last refresh over one quarter old) or with a missing required document is logged as an exception

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off the file as exam-ready after every quarterly refresh or exam-call-letter trigger

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All LOB/state exam readiness files maintained by the team, plus any file activated by a real exam call letter in the test period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any file more than one full quarter stale, or missing a required document category, is a fail; any real exam response missing its stated deadline is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; test runs quarterly, timed to just after the quarterly refresh checkpoint

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not be the assigned owner of any sampled file

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly exam readiness test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The exam readiness file itself, self-tested by mock exam, is the regulator-ready documentation

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager is the single point of contact for any state exam call letter; Regulatory Counsel and Head of Compliance are looped in within 1 business day of receipt

checklist.step: Define the required document inventory per LOB/state file
actions: List the standard exam readiness document categories: written procedures, current and prior 2 years' MCAS submissions, complaint log with dispositions, a sample set of closed claim files, a sample set of underwriting/policy files, producer appointment/termination records, and responses to any prior exam.
Confirm the category list against the current NAIC Market Regulation Handbook examiner document-request checklist.
Publish the inventory checklist to the GRC platform as the file's table of contents.
checklist.done: the required document inventory is defined, checked against the NAIC Handbook, and published as the file's table of contents.

checklist.step: Assign an owner per LOB/state file
actions: Assign a named owner (typically a Compliance Analyst) for each LOB/state exam readiness file.
Confirm the owner has read access to the Claims Platform, Policy Administration Platform, workflow/case management tool and agency/producer management system needed to refresh the file.
Record the owner assignment in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: every LOB/state file has a named, access-confirmed owner recorded in the GRC platform.

checklist.step: Pull the current procedures and MCAS submissions into the file
actions: Copy the current approved conduct-area procedures from the procedure library into the exam readiness file.
Copy the current and prior two years' MCAS submission confirmations and SDR extracts for the LOB/state into the file.
Timestamp the copy date on each document.
checklist.done: current procedures and three years of MCAS submissions are copied into the file with copy timestamps.

checklist.step: Refresh the complaint log extract
actions: Pull the full complaint log for the LOB/state for the trailing 3 years from the workflow/case management tool, including received date, category, resolution and closure date.
Confirm the extract ties to the complaint counts reported in the most recent MCAS submission.
Save the refreshed extract into the file, replacing the prior quarter's copy.
checklist.done: the complaint log extract is refreshed, tied to the MCAS-reported counts, and dated.

checklist.step: Draw a rotating sample of closed claim files
actions: In the Claims Platform, pull a random sample of at least 25 closed claims for the LOB/state from the trailing 12 months, including denials, closed-without-payment and paid claims in proportion to the book.
Export the full claim file (notes, correspondence, payment/denial letters) for each sampled claim.
Load the sample into the exam readiness file, replacing last quarter's sample.
checklist.done: a fresh random sample of at least 25 closed claim files, proportional to the book, is loaded into the file.

checklist.step: Draw a rotating sample of underwriting/policy files
actions: Pull a random sample of at least 25 new business and renewal policy files for the LOB/state from the trailing 12 months, including any declinations and nonrenewals.
Export underwriting notes, rating worksheets and any adverse-action notices for each sampled file.
Load the sample into the exam readiness file, replacing last quarter's sample.
checklist.done: a fresh random sample of at least 25 underwriting/policy files, including declinations and nonrenewals, is loaded into the file.

checklist.step: Refresh producer appointment/termination records
actions: Pull current appointment, termination and for-cause termination records for producers active in the LOB/state from the agency/producer management system.
Confirm termination records include the reason code and notification date sent to the state (as required for for-cause terminations).
Load the refreshed extract into the file.
checklist.done: current producer appointment and termination records, with reason codes and notification dates, are loaded into the file.

checklist.step: Attach any prior exam response materials
actions: Locate the response package from the most recent market conduct exam for the LOB/state, if any occurred in the last 5 years.
Confirm the response package includes the exam report, the company's response letter and any corrective action closure evidence.
Attach or link the package in the exam readiness file.
checklist.done: any prior exam's response package, report and corrective action closure evidence is attached or linked in the file.

checklist.step: Run a quarterly completeness check against the document inventory
actions: Check off each required document category in the GRC platform's file checklist as refreshed and confirmed current.
List any category not refreshed within the quarter or missing entirely.
Route missing/stale categories back to the responsible owner with a 5-business-day cure window.
checklist.done: the quarterly completeness check is recorded with every category checked off or routed for a 5-day cure.

checklist.step: Run a mock-exam self-test
actions: Once per year, role-play a state examiner's opening document request using the current NAIC Market Regulation Handbook checklist against one LOB/state file.
Time how long it takes to produce every requested document from the file as maintained.
Note any document that could not be produced within the state's typical 10-30 day response window and report it to Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: the annual mock-exam self-test is run with a documented response time and any gap reported.

checklist.step: Set up the exam-call-letter immediate-refresh trigger
actions: Configure a GRC platform workflow that, on logging any exam call letter, immediately assigns a same-day high-priority refresh task to the relevant LOB/state file owner.
Test the trigger by logging a dummy call letter in a sandbox record and confirming the task fires.
Remove the dummy record after testing.
checklist.done: the exam-call-letter trigger is configured and proven to fire a same-day refresh task.

checklist.step: Confirm continuous access controls on the file
actions: Review the GRC platform's access list for each exam readiness file quarterly, confirming only current file owners and Compliance leadership have write access.
Remove access for any staff no longer in the assigned role.
checklist.done: file access is confirmed limited to current owners and leadership, with departed staff removed, each quarter.

checklist.step: Log stale or incomplete files as exceptions
actions: At each quarterly checkpoint, list any LOB/state file more than one quarter stale or missing a required document category past its cure window.
Open a tracker issue with root cause and an owner for each.
Set a remediation date within 10 business days.
checklist.done: every stale or incomplete file has a tracker issue with root cause, owner and a 10-business-day remediation date.

checklist.step: File the quarterly refresh evidence
actions: Upload the quarterly completeness check, sample document lists and any mock-exam self-test results to the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label and index by LOB and state.
checklist.done: quarterly refresh evidence is filed, retention-labelled and indexed by LOB and state.

checklist.step: Obtain quarterly sign-off that files are exam-ready
actions: Review the completeness check and any open exceptions for the quarter.
Sign the quarterly exam-readiness attestation confirming every file is current, or listing named exceptions with remediation dates.
File the attestation with the evidence package.
checklist.done: a signed quarterly exam-readiness attestation, naming any exceptions and remediation dates, is filed with the evidence package.

testing.step: Build the population of maintained exam readiness files
actions: List every LOB/state exam readiness file the team maintains, from the GRC platform's file registry.
Reconcile the file list to the full LOB/state population reported in the most recent MCAS submission to confirm no combination is missing a file.
testing.done: the maintained-file population is reconciled to the MCAS submission's LOB/state list.

testing.step: Reconcile refresh dates to the quarterly checkpoint
actions: Pull the last-refresh date recorded in the GRC platform for every file.
List any file not refreshed within the most recent quarter as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every file's refresh date is checked against the quarter, with stale files listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of files flagged stale or that had a real exam call letter in the test period.
Take a random sample of at least 8 additional files, seeded and reproducible.
Record the seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: the sample covers all stale/exam-triggered files plus a documented random selection.

testing.step: Test document completeness against the required inventory
actions: For each sampled file, check every required document category against the actual contents in the GRC platform.
Confirm claim and policy file samples meet the minimum 25-item size and cover declinations/denials in proportion to the book.
Log any missing category or undersized sample as an exception.
testing.done: document completeness against the required inventory is confirmed for every sampled file, or gaps are logged.

testing.step: Verify the complaint log ties to the MCAS submission
actions: For each sampled file, compare the complaint log extract's total count to the complaint count reported in the corresponding MCAS submission for the same period.
Investigate and log any material variance.
testing.done: complaint log totals are confirmed to tie to the MCAS submission for every sampled file, or variances are logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the mock-exam timing test
actions: Independently role-play a document request against 2 sampled files using the current NAIC Market Regulation Handbook checklist.
Time production and compare against the state's typical 10-30 day response window.
Log any document that could not be produced timely.
testing.done: an independent mock-exam timing test is run on 2 sampled files with results compared to the regulatory response window.

testing.step: Verify access controls on the sample
actions: Pull the current access list for each sampled file and compare to the list of current file owners and Compliance leadership.
Flag any access held by staff no longer in the assigned role.
testing.done: access lists are confirmed current for every sampled file, or gaps are flagged.

testing.step: Trace real exam call letters to the same-day trigger and response
actions: For any real exam call letter received in the test period, confirm the GRC platform trigger fired a same-day refresh task.
Confirm the file response met the state's stated deadline in the call letter.
Log any missed trigger or late response as a compliance breach, not a documentation exception.
testing.done: every real exam call letter in the period is traced to a same-day trigger and an on-time response, or a breach is logged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every stale file, incomplete document category, complaint-log variance, access gap or missed exam response.
Assign root cause and owner; missed real-exam deadlines route to Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel for a self-assessment.
Set remediation dates and carry open issues into next quarter's mandatory retest.
testing.done: every finding has a tracker issue with root cause, owner and remediation date, with missed exam responses self-assessed.

testing.step: Conclude and sign the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the one-quarter-staleness and completeness thresholds.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and have an independent reviewer who performed none of the sampled checks sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is reported to the Compliance Committee and filed in the compliance evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns remediation of every market conduct exam finding from receipt of the exam report through corrective action closure and regulator confirmation

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Massachusetts General Laws Chapters 174 to 176 market conduct exam and corrective action provisions, re-read at the time each exam report is received (rep: Kentucky KRS Chapter 304 for baseline exam authority)

In-scope processes.value: Exam finding intake, root cause analysis, corrective action plan drafting, regulator negotiation of timelines, implementation tracking and closure evidence, for every market conduct exam finding issued against any LOB/state

In-scope systems.value: Findings and corrective action plans tracked in the GRC platform; supporting evidence drawn from the Claims Platform, Policy Administration Platform and agency/producer management system as relevant to the finding

Compliance procedure documented.value: Exam Finding Remediation Procedure — intake, root cause, corrective action plan, regulator agreement, implementation tracking, closure verification

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Head of Compliance and General Counsel; reviewed annually

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per finding — the agreed timeline stated in the exam report or the negotiated corrective action plan (commonly 30-90 days for procedural findings, longer for system changes); tracked individually per finding in the GRC platform

Deadline reminders configured.value: T-30/T-14/T-7 day reminders to the finding owner and Compliance Manager ahead of each finding's agreed remediation date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Exam report, corrective action plan, implementation evidence and regulator closure confirmation retained 7 years from closure

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any finding remediated past its agreed date, or reopened by the regulator, is logged as an exception with root cause

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every finding before the closure letter is sent to the regulator

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All market conduct exam findings issued in the test period, plus any finding still open from a prior period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any finding remediated after its agreed date without a documented, regulator-approved extension is a fail; any finding reopened by the regulator is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; test runs on every finding at closure, plus a semi-annual review of all open findings

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have owned or implemented any sampled finding's corrective action

Evidence location for test results.value: Per-finding remediation test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The corrective action plan, implementation evidence and closure letter, presentable to the regulator on request

Regulator response path.value: Compliance Manager owns the closure letter and regulator correspondence; General Counsel clears the letter before it is sent

checklist.step: Log the exam finding on receipt
actions: On receipt of the market conduct exam report, create a finding record in the GRC platform for each individual finding, capturing the exam state, LOB, finding text, citation and the regulator's stated remediation deadline.
Attach the full exam report to the finding record.
Notify Head of Compliance and General Counsel within 1 business day of receipt.
checklist.done: every finding in the exam report has a GRC record with citation, deadline and the report attached, and leadership is notified within 1 business day.

checklist.step: Assign a root-cause owner per finding
actions: Assign each finding to the accountable business owner (Chief Claims Officer, Chief Underwriting Officer, Producer Licensing Coordinator, Complaints Manager, as the finding subject dictates).
Set a 10-business-day root-cause deadline for the owner.
Record the assignment and deadline on the finding record.
checklist.done: every finding has a named business owner and a 10-business-day root-cause deadline recorded.

checklist.step: Conduct root-cause analysis
actions: Working with the assigned owner, trace the finding to its underlying cause: procedure gap, system limitation, training gap, staffing/volume issue, or an isolated error.
Pull the transaction-level evidence the examiner cited (claim files, complaint records, producer files) and confirm the finding's factual basis.
Document the root cause and whether it is isolated or systemic (likely to recur across other files/states).
checklist.done: a documented root cause, confirmed against the examiner's cited evidence, classifies the finding as isolated or systemic.

checklist.step: Draft the corrective action plan
actions: For each finding, draft a corrective action plan with named actions (procedure change, system fix, training, file remediation), an owner and a target date per action.
For systemic findings, include a look-back scope defining which prior files/periods need remediation.
Route the draft plan to the accountable business owner and General Counsel for review.
checklist.done: every finding has a drafted corrective action plan with named actions, owners, target dates and, for systemic findings, a look-back scope.

checklist.step: Negotiate and confirm the agreed timeline with the regulator
actions: Submit the draft corrective action plan and proposed timeline to the examining state's market conduct division within the exam report's response window.
Negotiate any timeline that cannot realistically be met, documenting the regulator's counter-proposal or agreement in writing.
Record the final agreed date on the finding record, distinct from the original exam-report deadline if renegotiated.
checklist.done: the final agreed remediation date, confirmed in writing by the regulator, is recorded on the finding record.

checklist.step: Get Head of Compliance and General Counsel approval on the final plan
actions: Review the final corrective action plan and agreed timeline for adequacy and resourcing feasibility.
Obtain General Counsel sign-off that the plan and any regulator correspondence carry no unintended legal admission.
Sign the plan as approved before implementation begins.
checklist.done: Head of Compliance and General Counsel have signed the final corrective action plan before implementation starts.

checklist.step: Implement procedure and system-level actions
actions: Track each procedure or system action from the plan through to completion, updating the relevant conduct-area procedure or system configuration as specified.
Obtain the accountable business owner's confirmation that the change is live and operating.
Attach the updated procedure or system change record as evidence on the action.
checklist.done: every procedure/system action in the plan is completed with the business owner's confirmation and evidence attached.

checklist.step: Deliver training actions
actions: Deliver the training specified in the corrective action plan to the affected team.
Capture attendance and a post-training comprehension check where the finding involved a judgment error.
File the training materials and attendance log as evidence.
checklist.done: training is delivered with an attendance log and, where applicable, a comprehension check on file.

checklist.step: Remediate the look-back population for systemic findings
actions: Pull every file in the defined look-back scope (by LOB, state and period) from the relevant source system.
Re-review each file against the corrected standard and issue any owed payment, refund or corrected notice.
Log the remediation outcome (amount paid, notice sent, no action needed) per file in the remediation log.
checklist.done: every file in the look-back scope is re-reviewed with a logged outcome, and any owed payment or notice is issued.

checklist.step: Track implementation status against the agreed timeline
actions: Update the finding record in the GRC platform weekly with the status of every action in the plan.
Escalate any action trending late to Head of Compliance at least 14 days before the agreed date.
Request a documented regulator extension before the agreed date if an action cannot complete on time — never let a deadline pass silently.
checklist.done: the finding record shows weekly status updates, and any at-risk action is escalated at least 14 days ahead or has a documented regulator extension.

checklist.step: Assemble closure evidence
actions: Compile evidence that every action in the plan is complete: updated procedures, system change records, training logs, and the look-back remediation log.
Cross-check the evidence package against the plan line by line to confirm nothing is missing.
checklist.done: a complete, line-by-line-checked closure evidence package exists for the finding.

checklist.step: Obtain Head of Compliance closure sign-off
actions: Review the closure evidence package against the approved corrective action plan.
Sign the closure attestation confirming every action is complete and evidenced.
checklist.done: Head of Compliance has signed a closure attestation confirming every plan action is complete and evidenced.

checklist.step: Send the closure letter to the regulator
actions: Draft the closure letter summarizing the actions taken and referencing the agreed timeline met (or the approved extension used).
Route through General Counsel for final legal review before sending.
Submit the closure letter to the examining state's market conduct division and log the submission date.
checklist.done: the closure letter is legally reviewed, submitted to the regulator, and the submission date is logged.

checklist.step: Log any finding that missed its agreed date as an exception
actions: For any finding that passed its agreed date without a documented regulator extension, open a tracker issue with root cause and impact.
Assess whether the miss requires proactive disclosure to the regulator and route the assessment to General Counsel.
Set a new remediation date and track to closure.
checklist.done: every missed-deadline finding has a tracker issue with a disclosure assessment and a new tracked remediation date.

checklist.step: File the complete remediation record
actions: Upload the exam report, corrective action plan, all implementation evidence, the closure attestation and the regulator closure letter/confirmation to the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year-from-closure retention label.
Index the record by exam, LOB and state for future exam readiness file linkage.
checklist.done: the complete remediation record is filed, retention-labelled and indexed for exam readiness linkage.

testing.step: Build the population of exam findings
actions: Pull every market conduct exam finding logged in the GRC platform during the test period, plus any finding still open from a prior period.
Reconcile the finding count to the total findings listed in each underlying exam report.
testing.done: the finding population is reconciled to the count of findings in each exam report.

testing.step: Reconcile findings to corrective action plans and closure status
actions: Match every finding to a corrective action plan and a status (open, in progress, closed).
List any finding with no corrective action plan as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every finding is matched to a plan and status, or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of findings that missed their agreed date or were reopened by a regulator.
Take a random sample of at least 5 additional closed findings, seeded and reproducible.
Record the seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: the sample covers all missed/reopened findings plus a documented random selection of closed findings.

testing.step: Re-perform the root-cause and closure evidence review
actions: For each sampled finding, independently read the exam report language and compare it to the documented root cause and corrective action plan.
Confirm the plan's actions genuinely address the root cause rather than a symptom.
Log any plan judged inadequate to the finding as an exception.
testing.done: root cause and plan adequacy are independently re-reviewed for every sampled finding, with inadequate plans logged.

testing.step: Trace the agreed timeline to regulator correspondence
actions: For each sampled finding, locate the regulator correspondence confirming the agreed remediation date.
Confirm the date on the finding record matches the regulator-confirmed date, including any documented extension.
Log any mismatch or undocumented extension as an exception.
testing.done: the agreed date on each sampled finding record is confirmed to trace to regulator correspondence, or a mismatch is logged.

testing.step: Verify implementation evidence for each action
actions: For each sampled finding, check every corrective action plan line against its filed evidence (updated procedure, system change record, training log, look-back remediation log).
Confirm evidence dates are on or before the closure attestation date.
Log any action marked complete with no or post-dated evidence.
testing.done: implementation evidence is confirmed present and correctly dated for every action on every sampled finding, or gaps are logged.

testing.step: Re-perform a portion of the look-back remediation for systemic findings
actions: For sampled findings with a look-back scope, pull 10 files from the look-back population and independently confirm the file was re-reviewed and any owed payment/notice was issued per the remediation log.
Log any file in scope but missing from the remediation log.
testing.done: 10 look-back files per sampled systemic finding are independently confirmed remediated, or gaps are logged.

testing.step: Recompute deadline compliance across the full population
actions: Compare every finding's closure date (or current status if still open) to its agreed remediation date across the full population, not just the sample.
List every finding that missed its date without a documented extension as a breach.
testing.done: deadline compliance is computed for 100% of the finding population with breaches separately identified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every inadequate plan, evidence gap, undocumented extension or missed deadline found.
Assign root cause and owner; missed deadlines and reopened findings route to General Counsel for a disclosure assessment.
Carry every open finding into the next semi-annual retest until closed.
testing.done: every finding-level exception has a tracker issue with root cause, owner and remediation date, with breaches disclosure-assessed.

testing.step: Conclude and sign the test
actions: Compute the on-time closure rate and compare to the zero-missed-deadline-without-extension threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and have an independent reviewer who performed none of the sampled re-reviews sign the workpaper.
Report results and any reopened/missed finding to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and on-time closure rate is reported to the Compliance Committee and filed in the compliance evidence repository.
